objective: Add a ROS-free, deterministic quintic point-to-point trajectory generator for the UR5e motion stack. The generator is an internal planning primitive only: it proves configured position, velocity, acceleration, and jerk bounds for one joint-space move, but does not modify existing trajectory preflight, dispatch, Gazebo, MoveIt, schemas, evidence, or hardware behavior.
acceptance: A new ROS-free module creates a deterministic joint-space quintic point-to-point profile from an exact ordered joint schema, start positions, target positions, and explicit per-joint position/velocity/acceleration/jerk limits.

For every moving joint, duration is the maximum of 15*abs(delta)/(8*v_max), sqrt(10*abs(delta)/(sqrt(3)*a_max)), and cbrt(60*abs(delta)/j_max); all joints share that maximum duration. Missing, non-finite, non-positive, mismatched, or extra limits fail closed without fallback values.

The profile samples position, velocity, acceleration, and jerk analytically on the closed interval [0, duration]; negative, non-finite, and out-of-range sample times are rejected rather than clamped or extrapolated.
Start and target positions must be finite and within explicit bounds. A zero-displacement profile has duration zero and can only be sampled at time zero with zero derivatives.

The implementation imports neither ROS, Gazebo, MoveIt, nor hardware adapters; it creates no RobotCommand, FollowJointTrajectory, ActionResult, event, WorldState, VerificationResult, or execution claim.
Tests cover endpoint conditions, analytic midpoint values, duration selection, deterministic mapping normalization, zero displacement, invalid schemas/limits/positions, and out-of-domain sampling.
The focused motion tests and required repository checks pass with no changes outside allowed_paths.
evidence: Task Packet validation output with an exact allowed-path boundary.
Focused red and green pytest output proving the generator's mathematical and fail-closed behavior.
Full pure-Python motion test output and required repository check output.
A Git diff limited to the Task Packet, trajectory primitive, and its tests.
stop_conditions: Implementation requires a public contract/schema, existing preflight behavior, ROS/Gazebo/MoveIt adapter, launch/configuration, event/replay, or hardware change.
Complete acceleration or jerk bounds are unavailable and the implementation would need a guessed or implicit default.
The module would be used to issue a robot command before a separate controller-integration Task Packet is approved.
Required tests or checks fail for a reason that cannot be fixed inside allowed_paths.
